Research

Cleaning the whole house.

Presented at the International Conference on Real Estate Statistics 2026, Tokyo

Before a house price index comes the unglamorous part: turning hand-typed, fragmented addresses into reliable locations. I presented how address reconstruction and spatial matching lift the share of linked Budapest transactions from about half to about 93%.

View the slides Read the post

Research

From printed pages to balance sheets.

Presented at EABH 2025 and EHES 2025

The Magyar Compass is a Hungarian financial yearbook that ran from 1874 to 1944, printed on paper. In the Compass project I extract its financial tables: rules find the balance sheets, a vision-language model reads the hard ones, and every extraction is checked against the totals printed on the page.

View the slides Read the post

Research

Did markets see the war coming?

Published in Finance Research Letters

We used Kyle's model of informed and uninformed investors to ask when the conviction of a war showed up in prices. The answer: markets started pricing it about 50 days before the outbreak, around January 6.

About

Trained as a researcher, wired as a developer.

I am a researcher in economics and data science. My current research uses large language models to extract and validate structured information from unstructured sources, from vision-LLM pipelines that digitise historical bank balance sheets to NLP that measures how generative AI exposes occupations. Before that I built large-scale financial data pipelines at the European Central Bank, after several years of empirical research at the Central Bank of Hungary. I am finishing a PhD in Economics & Finance at ELTE. This website shares lecture slides and posts about my research.
